title: The e2e lane runs a deploy against the real daemon composition with a fake docker port behind it
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (item 5 of five). Consumer is task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde, whose DoD 5 requires "a Playwright journey against a REAL daemon (with a fake docker port behind the daemon)".

THE GAP, from worker-f72a1438's audit: the seam EXISTS but is not forwarded end to end. `daemon-command-async-entries.ts:69-77`, `:92` and `:202-214` already define `DeploymentDeploySeams` and forward real handler options - but `daemon-command-registry.ts:108-155` / `:290-306` and the v2 registry do not carry it through to the composition an e2e lane actually starts. So a journey can reach a real daemon, and that daemon cannot be given a fake docker.

WHY A FAKE DOCKER RATHER THAN REAL DOCKER IN THE LANE: a deploy runs `docker build`, optionally `docker save | ssh docker load`, and a health poll that waits out docker's own start-period. That is minutes of wall clock, a daemon on the lane host, and a container and port to leak. Epic rail 4 binds - anything this epic starts, it stops, on EVERY exit path - and a lane that leaks a container makes every later gate on this board inadmissible. The fake port keeps the DAEMON, the command edge, the ledger and the receipts real, and replaces only the process spawn.

WHAT MUST STAY REAL, because the consumer's journey certifies exactly this: the daemon process, the command plane, the offer wire, the durable receipts, and the refusal codes. **Only the docker/ssh/transfer spawns are faked.** A journey whose daemon is also faked proves nothing about the product and would retire the question the consumer row exists to answer.

NOT IN SCOPE: the journey itself and the card (the consumer's), the target reader, the deployment-state read, the target-binding control.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm test:e2e:browser`. Note it is `tsc -p ... && playwright test -c ...`, so quote the SPEC COUNT and not only the exit code - a typecheck failure means Playwright never ran. Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`.
definitionOfDone: The e2e lane can start a REAL daemon whose deploy spawns are backed by an injected fake, forwarded through the production composition path the lane actually uses - not through a test-only constructor. Name the exact composition seam and assert the injected port is the one the deploy reaches, by observing the fake being called rather than by trusting the wiring.

ONLY THE SPAWNS ARE FAKE. Assert that with the fake in place the deploy still goes through the real command edge, the real admission, the real ledger and the real receipt: the durable receipt is written and readable through the production read path. A journey whose daemon is also faked certifies nothing, and this clause is what stops the seam widening into one.

THE FAKE IS UNAVAILABLE OUTSIDE THE LANE. Assert the production composition with NO seam supplied still gets the real docker runner - a default that silently falls back to a fake would make every production deploy a no-op that reports success. Assert the default by observing which runner is composed, not by reading the code.

BOTH OUTCOMES ARE DRIVABLE: the fake can produce a successful deploy AND each refusal the engine can raise, so the consumer's journey can cover the failure paths without real infrastructure. Assert at least one success and one refusal reaching a durable receipt with its code verbatim.

NOTHING LEAKS ON ANY EXIT PATH, including the failing ones (epic rail 4). No container, no port, no temp directory, no daemon process survives the lane - asserted in teardown rather than at the end of a happy path. A leaked container makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test:e2e:browser` with its SPEC COUNT quoted and the exercising spec named - the script is `tsc && playwright test`, so a typecheck failure means zero specs ran and the exit code alone cannot tell you.
taskRails: ONLY THE SPAWNS ARE FAKE. The daemon, the command edge, the admission, the ledger and the receipts stay real. A journey whose daemon is faked retires the question the consumer row exists to answer.

THE PRODUCTION DEFAULT MUST BE THE REAL RUNNER. A composition that falls back to a fake when no seam is supplied turns every production deploy into a no-op that reports success - assert the default by observation.
NOTHING LEAKS ON ANY EXIT PATH, failures included (epic rail 4). Container, port, temp directory and daemon all die in teardown.
FORWARD THROUGH THE PRODUCTION COMPOSITION, not a test-only constructor. A seam the real lane cannot reach is a seam that proves nothing.
THE E2E SCRIPT HIDES A ZERO-SPEC RUN: `tsc -p ... && playwright test -c ...`. Quote the spec count and name the spec; a passing tsc with no matching spec looks like success.

comments.content:
TWO NOTES CARRIED FROM A DUPLICATE ROW I FILED IN ERROR AND ARCHIVED (task-1bee7227). Both are measurements, not scope changes (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-06).

1. THE COMPOSITION ALREADY HAS THE SHAPE TO FOLLOW - no new mechanism needed. `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` declares `StoreDependencyConfig` with optional injected config already: `schedule?: Pick<ScheduleConfig, "timer" | "resolve">`, `repositoryWorkspace?`, `affordanceMintId?`, `clock?`. A lane-supplied docker/ssh seam is the same pattern one entry wider. Inventing a second injection mechanism where this one fits would give the daemon two ways to be configured for tests.
The seam has to reach `productionDeployPorts()` (deploy-command.ts:91), which today hard-codes `docker: nodeDockerRunner` and `ssh: nodeSshRunner` with no substitution point.

2. THE DISCLOSURE CONSTRAINT, which matters for whichever row consumes this. A journey running on a fake docker seam proves the daemon COMPOSED AND DISPATCHED correctly. It does NOT prove a container ran, an image was built, or a URL served. The consuming row (task-84cd2e55) has DoD clauses about an operator seeing "where it went", so it must state plainly which half its journey proves - otherwise a green browser journey reads as evidence of a working deploy when it is evidence of a working dispatch.
Two guardrails worth keeping when you plan this: production must be unchanged when no seam is supplied (assert the default explicitly), and the seam must not be reachable from an environment variable or ambient default - a test door an operator's daemon could open is a production hazard rather than a test affordance.

Context for why this matters now: docker was absent from this host for most of 2026-09-05 and is present today (29.6.2). A browser journey depending on the host's docker goes red whenever the host loses it, which already parked task-3706b7e7's DoD 3 and task-99f364e3's docker-dependent clauses. A lane-injected seam makes the journey depend on the daemon's composition instead.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
HOW A FAKE REACHES A DAEMON THAT IS A SEPARATE PROCESS — the question the row's framing hides. The lane spawns the daemon: `spawnNode(args, cwd, env)` (daemon-children.ts:81-84) runs `apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts` as a Node CHILD. You cannot hand a `DeployPorts` OBJECT to another process, so "inject the fake" can only mean one of three things:

(a) An env-var flag read inside apps/daemon that swaps in a fake. REJECTED, and it is the dangerous one: it would put fake-selection code in the production bundle, and task rail 2 exists precisely because a composition that can fall back to a fake turns every production deploy into a no-op reporting success. The fake must not ship in apps/daemon at all.
(b) A test-only constructor called by the lane. REJECTED by task rail 4 — a seam the real lane cannot reach proves nothing, and it would bypass the composition the consumer's journey is supposed to certify.
(c) CHOSEN, and the lane already does this: `daemon-main.ts` loads its dependency provider FROM A PATH given on argv (`--dependencies=<module>`), and daemon-ports.ts:293-299 already switches that path between the production provider and a lane provider. `fixed-demo-goal-dependencies.ts` is the working template: it imports the PRODUCTION `createStoreDependencies`, wraps it, and re-exports. So the fake lives in tests/, the daemon is real, the command edge is real, and the only substituted thing is the spawn.

WHAT MUST BE BUILT IN PRODUCTION FOR (c) TO WORK. `DeploymentDeploySeams` already exists and `createAsyncCommandEntries` already consumes it (async-entries.ts:69-77, :92, :202) — but nothing carries it from `createStoreDependencies` down to that call. That forwarding is this row's entire production diff, and it is three small edits, not a feature.

HOW THE SPEC SCRIPTS THE FAKE ACROSS A PROCESS BOUNDARY. The spec cannot call into the child, so the lane provider reads its BEHAVIOUR from an env var the spec sets when spawning (success / build-failed / docker-unavailable / health-timeout). That variable is read only by the module under tests/, never by apps/daemon — keeping rail 2 intact.

DoD 3 BY OBSERVATION, not by reading code: `productionDeployPorts(...)` returns `docker: nodeDockerRunner`, so a daemon-side arm asserts REFERENCE IDENTITY against the exported real runner when no seam is supplied. That is observation of what was composed, and it fails loudly if a later edit adds a fallback.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE FAKE MUST NEVER SHIP IN apps/daemon (task rail 2). Keep every line of it under tests/. If you find yourself adding an env-var check inside apps/daemon that selects a fake, stop — that is the failure mode the rail names, and it would make a production deploy a no-op that reports success.
2. THE V2 PLANE IS EASY TO MISS. daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:71 calls `createDaemonCommandPorts` separately; forward the option there too or v1 gets the fake and v2 silently keeps the real runner. A lane that happens to use v1 would look green while the other plane is unwired.
3. TWO FILES ARE ALREADY PAST THE LINE CAP (composition 580, registry 531). Add ONLY the option and its forwarding. Splitting either is not this row's job and would collide with the several rows editing them.
4. A ZERO-SPEC E2E RUN LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS (task rail 5). `tsc && playwright test` — quote the SPEC COUNT and name your spec.
5. LEAKS MAKE THE WHOLE BOARD INADMISSIBLE (epic rail 4). The daemon child, its port, its store directory and any temp tree die in TEARDOWN, not at the end of a happy path. daemon-children.ts already ships `killTree` and `survivingChildren` — use them and assert `survivingChildren` is empty rather than trusting the kill.
6. DoD 3 IS THE ANTI-VACUITY CLAUSE and must be asserted by OBSERVATION — reference identity against the exported real runner when no seam is supplied. A test that merely reads the source, or that asserts the seam works when supplied, does not catch a fallback added later.
7. THE PREREQUISITE IS STILL IN FLIGHT. task-79f8c7c0 may change `productionDeployPorts`'s signature to `(store, projectId)` while you work. Read its completionSummary via epicSiblings; if it has not landed, your DoD-2 arm cannot bind a target and you should report rather than plant a target event by hand.
8. DO NOT WIDEN THE SEAM. `DeploymentDeploySeams` already carries `healthBudgetMs`, `pollMs` and `sleep` precisely so a timeout arm need not wait out docker's real start-period — use them rather than adding new knobs.
